title: Boot & shutdown
summary: Unexpected restarts, blue screens, shutdowns and slow start-ups.

events.title: System rebooted without shutting down cleanly
events.meaning: Windows restarted without a normal shutdown, for example after a crash, a power cut or a forced power-off.
events.causes: Power loss, overheating, a driver or hardware fault, or holding the power button.
events.next: Look for a blue screen record (event 1001) just after this one, then read the events logged in the minutes before the restart.

events.title: The previous shutdown was unexpected
events.meaning: Windows noted at start-up that the last shutdown did not finish properly.
events.causes: The same causes as an unexpected restart: a crash, a power problem or a forced power-off.
events.next: Check what was logged just before the restart, and check power and temperatures.

events.title: The Event Log service started (Windows booted)
events.meaning: The Event Log service starts early in every boot, so this event marks when Windows came up.
events.next: Use it as a marker: events just before it belong to the previous session.

events.title: The Event Log service stopped (clean shutdown)
events.meaning: The Event Log service stops late in a normal shutdown, so this event marks a clean shutdown.
events.next: If a restart has no matching 6006 before it, the shutdown was probably not clean.

events.title: Windows restarted after a blue screen
events.meaning: Windows hit a fatal error, showed a blue screen and restarted. The message holds the stop code.
events.causes: A faulty driver, bad memory or disk, overheating, or a damaged system file.
events.next: Note the stop code in the message and search for it. Update or roll back recent drivers and check memory and disk health.

events.title: A restart or shutdown was requested
events.meaning: A program or a user asked Windows to restart or shut down. The message names the process, the reason and the user.
events.causes: An update restart, a manual restart or a program that restarts the PC.
events.next: Read the message to see who asked and why.

events.title: Windows started
events.meaning: The operating system started. The message shows the Windows build.
events.next: Use it as a boot marker.

events.title: Windows is shutting down
events.meaning: The operating system began shutting down.
events.next: Use it as a shutdown marker.

events.title: Windows took longer than normal to start
events.meaning: Start-up was slower than the baseline Windows measures. The message shows the boot time and what slowed it down.
events.causes: Too many start-up programs, a slow disk, or a driver or service that starts slowly.
events.next: Open the event details to see which apps, drivers or services took longest, and disable or update them.

events.title: Windows took longer than normal to shut down
events.meaning: Shutdown was slower than the baseline Windows measures. The message names what delayed it.
events.causes: A program or service that does not close quickly, or a slow disk.
events.next: Open the event details to see which program or service delayed shutdown, then update or remove it.
